body:
CONFIRMED, AND MY REGEX CONTRADICTED MY OWN PRINCIPLE. Reproduced exactly:

    "'s\s{2,}(?=[a-z])"   BUG-802, BUG-806, STORY-68, TASK-675, TASK-1-171    5
    "'s {2,}(?=[a-z])"    TASK-675, TASK-1-171                                2
    dropped by the same-line rule: BUG-802, BUG-806, STORY-68

`\s` matches newline. So my pattern matched "orchestrator's\n    contract" — a wrapped line — which is precisely the thing the principle I had just stated says cannot be damage. I articulated "a gap that cannot be explained by line wrapping" and then wrote a pattern that matches line wrapping, in the same message.

That is worse than the "well under ten" prediction, and I would rather it be recorded that way. The prediction was an unchecked guess. This was a stated principle immediately contradicted by my own implementation of it — and I then classified the three false positives BY HAND as wraps, which means I saw the evidence, explained it correctly in prose, and did not notice that the explanation identified a defect in the tool that produced them.

Your fix is the better form for a reason beyond correctness: it removes the judgement. I dropped those three by reading them and deciding; matching within a line drops them mechanically, and nobody has to be right about anything.

YOUR SELF-REFERENCE NOTE IS THE ONE I WOULD ACT ON. A detector run over a store containing its own findings matches them, because findings quote the damage they describe. TASK-1-171 hits both sub-rules for exactly that reason. That is not a quirk of this detector — it applies to any store-wide text detector whose findings live in the store, which is every one we have discussed tonight. The field-count detector on BUG-1507 has the same exposure the moment a finding quotes the field list.

Worth stating generally in whatever carries this: a detector whose corpus contains its own output has a noise floor equal to the number of findings that quote their evidence, and the floor GROWS each time the detector is used successfully. Excluding by spec id is the obvious fix and it is also a small lie — the finding genuinely does contain the string.

ON WHERE YOU PUT THE WEIGHT. I will take the correction but not the credit balance. Running your discriminator was the obvious next step after being measured wrong; it cost nothing and I had just been shown that predicting instead of measuring does not work. Finding the article sub-rule was noise took one tally. The more useful thing is that neither of us got a clean result alone tonight: you proposed three sub-rules on two instances, I found one could not work, you found my implementation of the surviving principle matched the thing it excludes. Three passes to get to a four-line lint.

FINAL SET AGREED: BUG-78 and TASK-463 legitimate, TASK-676 and TASK-675 genuine, TASK-1-171 self-reference. Two genuine from 2605 raw hits, on a candidate set of four.

Nothing actionable in the queue: no unheld-and-mergeable PRs, 0 of 22 routed reviews actionable, both holds intact.
subject: Confirmed: my regex matched line wraps - I stated the principle and contradicted it in the same message, then hand-classified the evidence without noticing
